title: Upward trends
description: Verbos, sustantivos y adverbios para describir subidas en IELTS Writing Task 1.

cards.definition: To go up; an increase.
cards.example: The number of cyclists rose from 1,200 in 2010 to 3,400 in 2020.
cards.note: Verbo intransitivo: 'prices rose', nunca 'prices were risen'.

cards.definition: To become larger in number or amount; a rise.
cards.example: There was a significant increase in online sales, which doubled to $40 million.
cards.note: 'increase BY' = la diferencia; 'increase TO' = la cifra final.

cards.definition: To become larger gradually.
cards.example: The urban population grew steadily, reaching 6 million by 2015.

cards.definition: To go up gradually, often over a period.
cards.example: Unemployment climbed to 9% in the second quarter.

cards.definition: To rise very quickly to a high level.
cards.example: Smartphone ownership soared from 15% to 82% in just five years.
cards.warning: Úsalo sólo para subidas grandes y rápidas; si la subida es leve, suena exagerado.

cards.definition: A sudden, large increase.
cards.example: Ticket sales surged in July, peaking at 95,000.

cards.definition: To increase extremely quickly.
cards.example: Demand for home-delivery services rocketed from 2 million to 9 million orders in 2020.
cards.warning: Más periodístico; en Task 1 'soar' o 'rise dramatically' quedan más académicos.

cards.definition: To become two / three times as large.
cards.example: Spending on research doubled between 2005 and 2015, from £2bn to £4bn.

cards.definition: By a large amount and quickly.
cards.example: Car exports rose sharply after 2012, from 300,000 to 750,000 units.

cards.definition: At a regular, slow pace.
cards.example: Average life expectancy increased gradually, by about two years per decade.

cards.definition: By a very small amount.
cards.example: The share of rail freight grew marginally, from 11% to 12%.

cards.definition: By a noticeable or large amount.
cards.example: Visitor numbers were considerably higher in 2019 than in 2009.

cards.definition: A general pattern of increase over time.
cards.example: Overall, all three countries show a clear upward trend in internet use.

cards.definition: To return to a higher level after a fall.
cards.example: After dipping to 40% in 2009, the figure recovered to 55% by 2012.

cards.definition: To arrive at a particular level.
cards.example: The number of students reached a high of 12,000 in 2018.

title: Downward trends
description: Vocabulario para describir caídas y descensos con precisión.

cards.definition: To go down; a decrease.
cards.example: Coal consumption fell from 45% to 18% of total energy use.

cards.definition: To become smaller; a reduction.
cards.example: There was a 30% decrease in the number of landline subscriptions.

cards.definition: To become gradually less; a gradual fall.
cards.example: Newspaper readership declined steadily throughout the period.

cards.definition: To fall, often suddenly.
cards.example: Attendance dropped to just 2,000 in 2020.

cards.definition: To fall very quickly and by a large amount.
cards.example: The price of DVDs plummeted from $20 to $4 within a decade.
cards.warning: Reserva 'plummet' para caídas grandes; no lo uses para un 2%.

cards.definition: To fall suddenly and steeply.
cards.example: Profits plunged by 60% in the final quarter.

cards.definition: A small, temporary fall.
cards.example: There was a slight dip in sales in March before they recovered.

cards.definition: To become smaller in size or amount.
cards.example: The agricultural workforce shrank from 20% to 5% of the population.

cards.definition: To reduce to half the original amount.
cards.example: The number of smokers halved between 1990 and 2020.

cards.definition: Describing a large, rapid change.
cards.example: The chart shows a steep decline in fish stocks after 2005.

cards.definition: A general pattern of decrease over time.
cards.example: Both regions followed a downward trend, although the fall was steeper in the north.

cards.definition: To reach the lowest point before stabilising or rising.
cards.example: House prices bottomed out at £150,000 in 2011 and then began to rise.

cards.definition: To decrease gradually towards the end of a period.
cards.example: Demand tailed off towards the end of the year, finishing at 300 units.

cards.definition: The act or result of making something smaller.
cards.example: There was a considerable reduction in water use, from 150 to 110 litres per person.
cards.note: Lo más natural es 'a reduction IN water use'; 'reduction OF' se usa sobre todo con la cifra: 'a reduction of 10%'.

cards.definition: To reach the lowest figure in the period.
cards.example: Interest rates hit a low of 0.5% in 2014.

title: Stability & fluctuation
description: Cómo decir que una cifra se mantiene estable o sube y baja.

cards.definition: To stay at about the same level.
cards.example: The proportion of part-time workers remained stable at around 25%.

cards.definition: To stop rising or falling and stay at a similar level.
cards.example: After rising rapidly, the number of users levelled off at 8 million.

cards.definition: To reach a level and stay there; a flat period.
cards.example: Sales reached a plateau of about 500 units a month between May and August.

cards.definition: To become steady after a period of change.
cards.example: The exchange rate stabilised at 1.2 dollars to the euro.

cards.definition: To stay exactly the same.
cards.example: The price of a bus ticket remained unchanged at $2 throughout the decade.

cards.definition: To stop changing and become level.
cards.example: The curve flattens out after 2016, hovering just below 40%.

cards.definition: To stay close to a particular figure.
cards.example: Inflation hovered around 2% for most of the period.

cards.definition: To rise and fall irregularly.
cards.example: Rainfall fluctuated between 40mm and 90mm per month.

cards.definition: An irregular rise and fall.
cards.example: Despite minor fluctuations, oil imports stayed close to 2 million barrels a day.

cards.definition: Changing often and unpredictably.
cards.example: Coffee prices were highly volatile, swinging between $1.10 and $2.40.

cards.term: a series of ups and downs
cards.definition: A pattern of repeated small rises and falls.
cards.example: Membership went through a series of ups and downs before settling at 3,000.

cards.definition: To come to rest at a level after changing.
cards.example: After some volatility, the figure settled at 65%.

cards.definition: To move regularly between two levels.
cards.example: Daily temperatures oscillated between 12°C and 18°C.

cards.definition: To change only very slightly.
cards.example: Figures for Japan showed little change over the 20-year period.

cards.definition: To keep at the same level.
cards.example: The company maintained a market share of roughly one third.

title: Peaks & troughs
description: Para señalar los puntos más altos y más bajos de un gráfico.

cards.definition: To reach the highest point; the highest point.
cards.example: Electricity demand peaked at 42 gigawatts at 6pm.

cards.definition: The lowest point on a graph.
cards.example: Visitor numbers reached a trough of 1,500 in February.

cards.definition: The maximum figure.
cards.example: Car sales hit a high of 2.3 million in 2007.

cards.definition: The minimum figure.
cards.example: The birth rate fell to a record low of 1.2 children per woman.

cards.definition: To arrive at the highest / lowest value.
cards.example: Water levels reached a maximum of 4.5 metres in April.

cards.definition: A sudden, short-lived sharp increase.
cards.example: There was a spike in website traffic in November, linked to a sales event.

cards.definition: To reach the highest level before stopping or falling.
cards.example: Enrolment topped out at 15,000 before declining.

cards.definition: To reach a maximum and then decrease.
cards.es: alcanzar un pico antes de volver a bajar
cards.example: Unemployment peaked at 12% in 2013 before falling back to 7%.
cards.note: Estructura útil para describir dos movimientos en una frase.

cards.definition: To reach the lowest point before recovering.
cards.example: The index bottomed out at 3,100 points in March.

cards.definition: The moment when a trend changes direction.
cards.example: The year 2008 marked a turning point, after which investment declined.

cards.term: the highest figure was recorded in
cards.definition: A passive structure to report the maximum.
cards.es: la cifra más alta se registró en
cards.example: The highest figure was recorded in Canada, at 78%.

cards.definition: To become higher than another line.
cards.example: Online sales overtook in-store sales in 2019, reaching 52%.

cards.definition: When two lines meet / come together.
cards.example: The two lines intersect in 2014, when both figures stood at 30%.

cards.definition: When two lines move further apart.
cards.example: From 2010 onwards, the figures for men and women diverged sharply.

cards.definition: The difference between two figures increased / decreased.
cards.example: The gap between urban and rural incomes narrowed from 40% to 25%.

title: Proportions & fractions
description: Cómo convertir porcentajes en fracciones y hablar de proporciones (gráficos de tarta y tablas).

cards.definition: A part of a whole, often in %.
cards.example: The proportion of households with a car rose to 70%.

cards.definition: The part of a total belonging to one category.
cards.example: Wind accounted for the largest share of renewable energy, at 41%.

cards.definition: To form a particular part of a total.
cards.example: Students accounted for 35% of library users, while retirees made up a further 20%.
cards.warning: No 'account of'. Y en activa: 'X accounts for 30%'.

cards.definition: To form or be part of a whole.
cards.example: Women constituted almost half of the workforce in 2020.
cards.warning: 'comprise' = 'consist of'; evita 'is comprised of' si buscas máxima corrección.

cards.definition: More / less than half.
cards.example: The vast majority of respondents (86%) preferred online banking.

cards.es: una cuarta parte / tres cuartas partes
cards.example: Exactly a quarter of the budget (25%) was spent on salaries.
Roughly two thirds of commuters (66%) travelled by car.
Half of all waste was recycled in 2020, compared with only 12% in 2000.

cards.term: one in five / one in ten
cards.definition: 20% / 10%, expressed as a ratio.
cards.example: One in five adults (20%) reported doing no exercise at all.

cards.definition: A very small part of.
cards.example: Nuclear power produced only a fraction of the electricity generated by coal.

cards.definition: The unit for the arithmetic difference between two percentages.
cards.example: The unemployment rate fell by three percentage points, from 10% to 7%.
cards.warning: De 10% a 7% es una bajada de 3 puntos porcentuales, NO de un 3%.

cards.definition: The relationship between two amounts.
cards.example: The ratio of students to teachers was 20 to 1.
collocations: a ratio of X to Y

cards.definition: Shared in equal parts.
cards.example: Opinion was evenly split, with 48% in favour and 48% against.

cards.definition: The part that is left.
cards.example: Rice made up 60% of the diet, with the remainder consisting of vegetables and fish.

cards.definition: The smallest / largest part of a pie chart.
cards.example: Transport formed the smallest segment, at just 4% of household spending.

title: Approximation
description: Expresiones para dar cifras aproximadas sin repetir siempre 'about'.

cards.definition: Close to a figure but not exactly.
cards.example: Roughly 3,000 people attended the festival in 2015 (2,960).

cards.definition: Near a figure.
cards.example: The figure stood at around 45% throughout the decade.

cards.definition: A little less than.
cards.es: algo menos de, justo por debajo de
cards.example: Just under half of respondents (48%) owned a tablet.

cards.definition: A little more than.
cards.es: algo más de, justo por encima de
cards.example: Just over a quarter of the budget (27%) went on healthcare.

cards.definition: Very close to but not quite.
cards.example: Exports nearly doubled, from 5.1 to 9.8 billion dollars.

cards.definition: Considerably more / less than.
cards.es: muy por encima / muy por debajo de
cards.example: Well over half of the students (68%) lived on campus.

cards.definition: Used before a number to mean 'approximately'.
cards.example: Some 40,000 tonnes of waste were produced annually.

cards.definition: Approximately.
cards.example: Annual costs were in the region of £2 million.

cards.definition: More than.
cards.example: Sales were in excess of 500,000 units in each of the final three years.

cards.term: a little over / a little under
cards.definition: Slightly more / less than.
cards.example: A little under a fifth of the land (18%) was used for farming.

cards.definition: Placed after a number to show approximation.
cards.example: Prices rose by 10% or so in the first year.
cards.warning: Coloquial: mejor para Speaking que para Task 1.

cards.definition: Almost reaching a figure.
cards.example: By 2020, the figure was close to 90%.

cards.definition: Varying between two limits.
cards.es: que oscila entre X e Y
cards.example: Rents varied widely, ranging from $600 to $2,100 a month.

cards.definition: Used to stress an exact figure.
cards.example: Precisely 50% of participants completed the course.

cards.definition: By a very small difference.
cards.example: The figure for boys was marginally higher than that for girls (51% vs 49%).

title: Comparison & contrast
description: Estructuras para comparar categorías y países en Task 1.

cards.definition: Used to compare two figures.
cards.example: Spain recorded 60 million tourists, compared with 35 million in Italy.

cards.definition: Introduces a contrasting fact in the same sentence.
cards.example: Car use rose by 20%, whereas bus use fell by 15%.

cards.definition: Double the number or amount of another.
cards.example: Men spent twice as much time on sport as women (6 hours vs 3).
cards.warning: 'many' con contables, 'much' con incontables. 'Twice more than' es incorrecto o ambiguo.

cards.definition: Multiplying comparison.
cards.example: Per capita energy consumption in the USA was four times higher than in India.

cards.definition: In the order already mentioned.
cards.example: France and Germany recorded 32% and 27% respectively.
cards.note: Ahorra palabras al dar dos cifras.

cards.definition: Almost or exactly equal to.
cards.example: The figure for Canada was similar to that for Australia, at around 18%.
cards.note: 'that of / those of' evita repetir el sustantivo.

cards.definition: Introduces an opposite fact.
cards.example: Rural areas saw falling populations. By contrast, cities grew by 30%.

cards.definition: To show the same kind of trend.
cards.example: Sales of tea and coffee followed a similar pattern, both peaking in winter.

cards.definition: To be more numerous than.
cards.example: Female students outnumbered male students by three to two.

cards.definition: To be greater than.
cards.example: In every year, imports exceeded exports.

cards.definition: To be lower than or slower than another.
cards.example: Rural internet access lagged behind urban access by around 20 percentage points.

cards.term: the highest / the lowest / the most
cards.definition: The top or bottom of a group.
cards.es: el más alto / el más bajo
cards.example: Norway had the highest rate of electric car ownership, at 79%.
cards.note: 'by far the + superlativo' enfatiza la diferencia.

cards.definition: Modifiers that show the size of a difference.
cards.example: Spending in 2020 was considerably lower than in 2010.

cards.definition: Shows that one figure is lower.
cards.example: Rail travel was not as popular as air travel, at 22% compared with 41%.

cards.definition: The opposite situation occurred.
cards.example: Men preferred football to tennis, whereas the reverse was true for women.

title: Process & map language
description: Secuenciadores, pasiva y lenguaje de ubicación y cambio para diagramas de proceso y mapas.

cards.definition: Introduces the first stage.
cards.example: To begin with, the raw cocoa beans are harvested and dried in the sun.

cards.definition: Introduces the following stage.
cards.example: Subsequently, the dried beans are transported to a factory.

cards.definition: After a step has been completed.
cards.es: una vez que, después de que
cards.example: Once the bottles have been cleaned, they are refilled and labelled.

cards.definition: Introduces the last stage.
cards.es: por último, en la etapa final
cards.example: In the final stage, the packaged tea is distributed to supermarkets.

cards.definition: The passive voice, used because the agent is unimportant.
cards.example: The clay is shaped into bricks, which are then fired in a kiln at 1,000°C.
cards.note: En procesos, la pasiva es casi obligatoria.

cards.definition: Language for cyclical processes.
cards.example: The water evaporates, forms clouds and falls as rain, and the cycle then begins again.

cards.definition: Used in the overview of a process.
cards.example: Overall, the production of glass consists of six stages, from collection to remoulding.

cards.definition: One feature took the place of another.
cards.example: The old fish market was replaced by a shopping centre in 2010.

cards.definition: Changed in use or form.
cards.example: The factory was converted into luxury flats.

cards.definition: Was destroyed on purpose.
cards.example: The warehouses were demolished to make way for a car park.

cards.definition: Was made or put up.
cards.example: A new bridge was constructed across the river to the east of the village.

cards.definition: Was made larger or longer.
cards.example: The runway was extended southwards by 500 metres.

cards.term: to the north of / in the north
cards.definition: Locating features by compass direction.
cards.es: al norte de / en el norte
cards.example: A school was built to the north of the park, while the hospital remained in the south-east.
cards.warning: 'in the north' = dentro de la zona; 'to the north of X' = fuera, al norte de X.

cards.definition: Describing positions relative to other features.
cards.es: contiguo a / al lado de / enfrente de
cards.example: The new library is adjacent to the town hall and opposite the bus station.

cards.term: the area became more developed / residential
cards.definition: Overview sentence summarising map changes.
cards.es: la zona se urbanizó / se volvió más residencial
cards.example: Overall, the village became far more urbanised, with farmland giving way to housing.
